mapping_reviews.reason: Article 10 of the EU AI Act addresses the obligations of providers of general-purpose AI models, including requirements for technical documentation and training data. It does not specifically address the exclusion of institutional data from training or the provision of an opt-out mechanism for such data.

Article 13 of the EU AI Act pertains to transparency obligations for deployers of certain AI systems, such as providing information to users. It does not contain provisions related to the training data of AI models or the opt-out of institutional data.

Article 25(4) of the EU AI Act concerns the obligations of providers of high-risk AI systems to implement a quality management system. This article does not address the specific issue of excluding institutional data from training or providing an opt-out mechanism.

missing_mappings.reason: This article requires providers of high-risk AI systems to take appropriate data governance and management measures, which could include procedures for handling institutional data and opt-outs.

applicability_note: The control is applicable to providers of AI models that are trained on data that may include institutional data, particularly those that are considered high-risk or general-purpose AI models under the EU AI Act.
challenge_comment: The provided mappings are incorrect. The control statement concerns the exclusion of institutional data from AI model training and the provision of an opt-out mechanism. None of the reviewed articles (10, 13, 25(4)) address this specific requirement. Article 29(1) is a more relevant provision as it mandates data governance measures for high-risk AI systems, which could encompass such data handling practices.
